topic_description: unsupervised graph embeddings using heat wavelet diffusion for structural role identification in networks

Heat Wavelet Diffusion for Dynamic Role.Problem: Existing graph embedding methods often struggle to capture the evolving structural roles of nodes in dynamic networks, where the topology and node attributes change over time.
Heat Wavelet Diffusion for Dynamic Role.Existing Methods: Current approaches like DeepWalk and node2vec primarily focus on static graphs and fail to account for temporal dynamics in role identification.
Heat Wavelet Diffusion for Dynamic Role.Motivation: Heat wavelet diffusion can model the propagation of information across a graph over time, potentially capturing the evolution of structural roles more effectively than static methods.
Heat Wavelet Diffusion for Dynamic Role.Proposed Method: We propose DynRoleWave, a novel unsupervised graph embedding framework that leverages heat wavelet diffusion to identify and track structural roles in dynamic networks. The method consists of three key components: 1) A time-dependent heat kernel that models the diffusion process across the evolving graph structure. 2) A wavelet transformation applied to the heat kernel to capture multi-scale structural information. 3) A recurrent neural network that learns to encode the temporal sequence of wavelet coefficients into dynamic role embeddings. The heat kernel is computed using a fast approximation method based on Chebyshev polynomials, allowing for efficient processing of large-scale graphs. The wavelet transformation uses a family of Mexican hat wavelets with varying scales to capture both local and global structural properties. The RNN encoder uses an attention mechanism to focus on the most relevant temporal patterns for role identification. The entire framework is trained end-to-end using a contrastive learning objective that encourages similar roles to have similar embeddings across time steps.
Heat Wavelet Diffusion for Dynamic Role.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate DynRoleWave on several real-world dynamic network datasets, including citation networks, social networks, and blockchain transaction graphs. We will compare against static baselines (DeepWalk, node2vec) and existing dynamic embedding methods (DynGEM, DynamicTriad) on tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and anomaly detection. We will also conduct qualitative analysis to visualize and interpret the learned dynamic roles.

Multi-View Graph Fusion for Structural R.Problem: Real-world networks often have multiple types of relationships between nodes, leading to multi-view graph data. Existing methods for structural role identification typically focus on single-view graphs, failing to leverage the rich information across different views.
Multi-View Graph Fusion for Structural R.Existing Methods: Current approaches like RolX and struc2vec are designed for single-view graphs and cannot directly handle multi-view data.
Multi-View Graph Fusion for Structural R.Motivation: Fusing information from multiple graph views can potentially lead to more robust and comprehensive structural role representations, capturing complementary aspects of node behaviors across different relationship types.
Multi-View Graph Fusion for Structural R.Proposed Method: We introduce MultiRoleFusion, a novel unsupervised framework for learning structural role embeddings from multi-view graph data. The method consists of four main steps: 1) View-specific embedding: For each graph view, we compute initial embeddings using a heat wavelet diffusion process, capturing structural information at multiple scales. 2) Cross-view attention: We employ a graph attention mechanism to learn the importance of each view for every node, allowing for adaptive fusion of information. 3) Embedding fusion: The view-specific embeddings are combined using the learned attention weights, resulting in a unified representation for each node. 4) Role clustering: We apply a differentiable clustering layer that learns to group the fused embeddings into distinct structural roles. The entire pipeline is trained end-to-end using a combination of reconstruction loss (to preserve view-specific information), cross-view consistency loss (to encourage agreement between views), and clustering loss (to discover well-separated roles). We also incorporate a novel regularization term that encourages the learned roles to be interpretable by favoring sparse associations between nodes and roles.
Multi-View Graph Fusion for Structural R.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate MultiRoleFusion on several multi-view network datasets, including multi-relational social networks, heterogeneous information networks, and multi-layer biological networks. We will compare against single-view baselines (RolX, struc2vec) applied to aggregated graphs, as well as existing multi-view embedding methods (MNE, DMGI) on tasks such as node classification, link prediction across views, and role-based community detection. We will also conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the contribution of each component in our framework.
